summary: Evidence GC deletes with its host's own login and no lock window: the evidence-tags ruleset keeps update and non_fast_forward and drops deletion. Every open pull request head keeps its records at any age (scripts/evidence-gc --open-heads-from, which the timer reads from the GitHub API). branch_days is 14, and cap_records is sized so the main window no longer exits 3. On the remote a dead group goes whole or not at all: duplicate names first, then each group in one atomic push.

replay.detail: No record, signature or verifier rule changes.

schema.detail: --lock-config and --relock-only are gone, and so is scripts/evidence-gc-lock.example.json. New --open-heads-from FILE takes one commit id a line. The summary gains live_trees.open_pull_requests, deleted_refs and kept_by_protection; it no longer has lock.

rules.detail: An open pull request head's tree is always live. Live branch tips are now those of the last 14 days, not 30. A push the remote's protection refuses (GH013) keeps its groups whole and is reported, not failed. The local refs follow exactly what the remote deleted.

compatibility.detail: An installed evidence-gc-timer from before this change passes --lock-config, which main's evidence-gc now refuses (exit 2, nothing deleted) until the new wrapper and unit are installed.

manual.detail: On the GC host: copy scripts/evidence-gc-timer to ~/.local/bin and scripts/evidence-gc.service to ~/.config/systemd/user, then run systemctl --user daemon-reload and remove ~/.config/evidence-gc/lock.json. On GitHub: drop the deletion rule from the evidence-tags ruleset, as .github/repo-settings.json declares.

recovery.detail: Revert the change and put the deletion rule back: GC then deletes no tag (each dead group is kept whole) until a lock window returns.
